title: Tambora eruption, 1815

place.label: Mount Tambora, Indonesia
place.basis: NCEI published volcano point for event 367; one point stands for a whole volcano
place.coords_source: NOAA NCEI Significant Volcanic Eruptions Database, event 367

date.label: Eruption date in the NCEI catalogue

facts.text: NCEI files Tambora as a stratovolcano and links this eruption to a tsunami record.
USGS says the 1991 Pinatubo eruption disturbed the atmosphere probably less than Krakatau 1883 and Tambora 1815 did; sulfate aerosols from big eruptions cool the climate.

tiers.everyday: In April 1815 Mount Tambora in Indonesia erupted. Tens of thousands of people died, many of them later from hunger, and USGS says its effect on the atmosphere was probably bigger than that of Pinatubo in 1991.
tiers.student: NOAA NCEI rates the eruption of 10 April 1815 at VEI 7, the highest in this batch, and counts 11,000 direct deaths and 60,000 in total. The USGS deadliest-eruptions table gives 92,000, mainly from starvation. The two totals disagree, so both are shown.
